title: ZenaTech Targets Adjusted EBITDA Breakeven in 2027 Following 425% First-Half Revenue Growth
summary: ZenaTech Targets Adjusted EBITDA Breakeven in 2027 Following 425% First-Half Revenue Growth Preliminary Q3 2026 revenue estimate of C$13.4–C$14.8 million […]
body_markdown:
***Preliminary Q3 2026 revenue estimate of C$13.4–C$14.8 million (US$9.5–US$10.5 million), representing 44%–59% sequential growth, as management balances breakeven target with strategic growth opportunities***


**Vancouver, British Columbia, (October 26, 2026)** — ZenaTech, Inc. (Nasdaq: ZENA) (FSE: 49Q) (BMV: ZENA) (“ZenaTech” or the “Company”), a technology solution provider specializing in AI (Artificial Intelligence) drone, Drone as a Service (DaaS), enterprise SaaS, and Quantum Computing solutions, announces that management is targeting 2027 as a potential breakeven year based on an adjusted EBITDA (a non-IFRS measure defined below). This operational target is supported by revenue growth, expansion of its DaaS operations, and anticipated operating efficiencies. In the first half of 2026, the Company reported revenue of C$17.7 million (approximately US$12.6 million). For the third quarter of 2026, the Company announced preliminary revenue estimates of C$13.4 million to C$14.8 million (approximately US$9.5 million to US$10.5 million), while retaining flexibility to pursue strategic growth opportunities.


“We believe ZenaTech is entering an important phase in its development,” said Shaun Passley, Ph.D., CEO of ZenaTech. “During the first half of 2026, we generated more revenue than during all of 2025, and our preliminary third-quarter estimates indicate that our growth trajectory will continue. We believe this expanding revenue base, together with operational efficiencies and acquisition integration, creates an opportunity for operational breakeven during 2027.”


The Company intends to maintain flexibility to invest in acquisitions, defense technologies, international operations, and emerging commercial opportunities that could defer breakeven while potentially generating greater long-term shareholder value.


**Second-Quarter and First-Half 2026 Financial Results**


**Metric** **Q2 2026** **First Half 2026**


**Total Revenue** C$9.33 million (US$6.6 million) C$17.73 million (US$12.6 million)


**Year-over-year revenue growth** 316% 425%


**DaaS revenue** C$8.63 million (US$6.1 million) C$16.44 million (US$11.7 million)


**Net loss** C$22.54 million (US$16.0 million) C$49.09 million (US$34.8 million)


**Operating expenses** C$31.24 million (US$22.1 million) C$61.21 million (US$43.4 million)


*US$ approximate conversions at US$0.709 per C$1.00, except where previously announced by the Company.*


First-half revenue exceeded the Company’s reported C$12.9 million (US$9.1 million) of revenue for all of 2025 by approximately 37%. DaaS operations accounted for 93% of first-half 2026 revenue. At June 30, 2026, the Company reported C$34.6 million (US$24.5 million) in cash and marketable securities, C$149.3 million (US$105.9 million) in total assets, and C$91.4 million (US$64.8 million) in shareholders’ equity.


Management recognizes that sustained revenue growth must translate into improved operating efficiency and financial performance. Reported net losses underscore the importance of controlling costs and assessing the returns on future investments.


“Our focus is increasingly on translating revenue growth into improved operating performance while building a technology platform capable of supporting a significantly larger business,” continued Dr. Passley.


**Preliminary Third -Quarter 2026 Revenue Estimates** ZenaTech previously announced preliminary, unaudited third -quarter 2026 revenue estimates of C$13.4 million to C$14.8 million. Compared with second -quarter revenue, this implies approximately 44% to 59% sequential revenue growth. Combined with reported first -half results, estimated revenue for the first nine months of 2026 would be approximately C$31.1 million to C$32.5 million (US$22.1 million to US$23.0 million).


These estimates are preliminary, unaudited, and subject to quarter-end close and reporting procedures. The Company also previously reported average organic revenue growth of 27.1% across approximately 20 DaaS locations acquired in 2025, excluding 2026 acquisitions.


**Maintaining Flexibility to Capture Growth Opportunities** While management has established 2027 as a target year for breakeven, ZenaTech does not intend to limit strategically attractive investments solely to achieve profitability within a predetermined period. Potential opportunities include:


- Acquisitions of complementary Drone as a Service and technology businesses
- Government and defense drone programs, including testing, certification, and production capabilities
- Expansion into additional international markets
- Commercialization of autonomous drone technologies and AI-driven enterprise SaaS platforms
- Development of new drone-enabled services, analytics, and automation applications


“Achieving breakeven is an important objective, but we are not building ZenaTech for a single financial reporting period,” continued Dr. Passley. “If opportunities emerge to significantly accelerate our growth through acquisitions, government and defense programs, or new technology investments, we may choose to deploy additional capital even if doing so delays our breakeven timeline.


“We believe the appropriate measure of our success will be our ability to create a larger, stronger, and more sustainable business over time. Our capital allocation decisions will be guided by expected long-term returns, financial discipline, and shareholder value creation,” concluded Dr. Passley.


**2027 Financial Target Considerations** Management expects to focus on increasing revenue from existing operations, improving operating efficiencies, integrating acquisitions, and expanding technology-enabled services. Management’s ability to achieve Adjusted EBITDA breakeven in 2027 remains subject to assumptions and operational variables, including top-line execution, the pace and cost of M&A integration, supply chain conditions, operating expenditure controls, and market acceptance of new commercial technologies. This target represents an internal management planning goal and does not constitute a projection, forecast, or guarantee of future financial performance.


**Non-IFRS / Non-GAAP Financial Measures** This press release refers to Adjusted EBITDA, a financial measure not recognized under International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) or U.S. GAAP. The Company defines EBITDA as net income or loss before interest expense, income taxes, depreciation, and amortization. Adjusted EBITDA further excludes non-cash stock-based compensation, acquisition-related transaction and integration expenses, fair-value adjustments on financial instruments, restructuring costs, and other non-recurring or unusual items as disclosed in the Company’s periodic financial filings.


Management uses Adjusted EBITDA to assess core operating performance, evaluate underlying business trends, and establish internal budgetary targets. It is believed this measure provides investors with supplemental insight into operational results by removing items that are non-operational, non-cash, or non-recurring.


Adjusted EBITDA should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for, or superior to, IFRS net loss, operating profit, or cash flows from operating activities. Other companies may calculate Adjusted EBITDA differently, limiting its comparability.


**Reconciliation Limitation** :
The Company has not provided a forward-looking quantitative reconciliation of targeted 2027 Adjusted EBITDA to the most directly comparable IFRS measure (Net Income/Loss) because items that reconcile these metrics—including future share-based compensation, tax provisions, transaction-related fair value adjustments, and potential impairment charges—are dependent on future events, volatile, and inherently difficult to predict with reasonable accuracy without unreasonable effort. Consequently, such reconciling information is unavailable at this time, though these items could have a significant and potentially unpredictable impact on future IFRS results.


**About ZenaTech**[ZenaTech](https://www.zenatech.com/) , Inc. (Nasdaq: ZENA) (FSE: 49Q) (BMV: ZENA) is a technology company that specializes in AI autonomy drone platforms and services to transform commercial, government, and defense sectors. Its subsidiaries include drone manufacturing through ZenaDrone, a global[Drone as a Service](https://www.droneasaservice.com/) (DaaS) business, and an enterprise SaaS division. The Company is executing an acquisition-led DaaS strategy to digitize and automate legacy service industries like land surveys and inspections, driving drone-based scalable, recurring revenue growth. With an operating footprint spanning North America, Europe, the Middle East, Asia, and Australia, ZenaTech is advancing AI drones for applications such as agriculture and logistics, as well as ISR, cargo, and counter-UAS for U.S. defense and NATO allies. The company is investing in next-generation technologies, including drone swarms, quantum computing, and advanced AI autonomy to capture long-term opportunities in key markets through its R&D initiatives.


**About ZenaDrone** ZenaDrone, a subsidiary of ZenaTech, designs and manufactures vertically integrated AI-powered autonomous drone solutions which include machine learning, predictive analytics, and advanced computing technologies, for government, defense, and industrial applications. This includes multifunctional drones for surveying, inspections, logistics, security, and defense applications. Its product portfolio at various stages of development includes the[ZenaDrone 1000](https://www.zenatech.com/drone-technology-solutions/) for ISR defense and specialized cargo, the[IQ Nano](https://www.zenatech.com/drone-technology-solutions/) for indoor inventory management and security, the[IQ Square](https://www.zenadrone.com/zenadrone-iq-square/) for outdoor inspections and maintenance, the[IQ Quad](https://www.zenadrone.com/iq-quad-drone/) for land surveying, the IQ Aqua, for underwater applications, and the IQ Octo for precision agriculture. ZenaDrone operates three global manufacturing and assembly facilities in Arizona, Dubai, and Taiwan, and is advancing counter-UAS maritime interceptor drones and an integrated defense system.
